AP All-American Third Team (2010) }} '''Cole Aldrich''' (born October 31, 1988) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player from [[Bloomington, Minnesota]]. He completed his junior year at the [[University of Kansas]] in March 2010. Aldrich was selected as a [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All American]] in 2006.[http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=24966&Sport=2 Rivals.com] He attended [[Bloomington Jefferson High School]]. Aldrich won the 2008 NCAA Championship and three Big 12 Championships during his time at Kansas. ==Collegiate career== ===Freshman season=== During the 2007-08 season at [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], Aldrich's freshman season, his playing time was limited due to playing behind future [[NBA Draft|NBA draft]] picks [[Darrell Arthur]], [[Sasha Kaun]], and [[Darnell Jackson]]. He averaged three rebounds and 2.8 points a game on 8.3 minutes a game during the regular season. Statistically, Aldrich's best performance was an 11-point, 11-rebound outing in a win over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]] on March 3, 2008.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=36170&year=2008 Cole Aldrich Kansas Jayhawks Game Log (2007-08)] Probably the most crucial game for Aldrich was during the Final Four game between Kansas and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] on April 5, 2008, when he played only 16 minutes but managed to grab 8 rebounds and score 7 points along with blocking 4 shots while also playing effective defense against National Player of the Year [[Tyler Hansbrough]], helping lead Kansas into the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA national championship game]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000031 North Carolina battles back, but Rush, Kansas close out Tar Heels]. ===Sophomore season=== With the departure of the other Jayhawk big men to the NBA draft, Aldrich became the premier big-man going into his sophomore season. Through the first 29 games, he averaged a double-double with 15.1 points and 10.8 rebounds in 29.7 minutes of play. He grabbed a career-high 20 rebounds in an 87-78 win over [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] on February 23, 2009,[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290540201 Taylor, Collins score 26 each as Jayhawks hand Sooners second straight loss]. On March 8, 2009, Aldrich was named to the 2008-09 Big 12 All-conference first team.{{cite web | last = Bedore | first = Gary | authorlink = http://www2.kusports.com/staff/gary_bedore | title = Jayhawks well-represented on coaches’ Big 12 teams | work = Lawrence Journal-World | publisher = The World Company | date = March 8, 2009 | url = http://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/mar/08/jayhawks-well-represented-coaches-big-12-teams/ | accessdate = March 9, 2009}} On March 22, 2009 Aldrich recorded the first official [[triple-double]] in the history of Kansas basketball against Dayton in the second round of the NCAA tournament. Aldrich accumulated 13 points, 20 rebounds, and 10 blocks in a 60-43 victory. [http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=294000056 Aldrich's 13 points, 20 boards, 10 blocked shots lead KU to Sweet 16]. On Monday, April 13, Aldrich announced he will return to KU for his Junior season. ===Junior season=== He won the 2009-10 men's college basketball [[Academic All-American]] of the Year as selected by [[CoSIDA]] and presented by ''[[ESPN the Magazine]]''.{{cite web|url=http://www.cosida.com/news/2010/2/22/0222105849_4996.aspx|title=Junior center Cole Aldrich of Kansas, Thomas More senior guard Daniel McKeehan lead ESPN the Magazine's Academic All-America® Men's Basketball Teams|accessdate=2010-02-23|date=2010-02-22|publisher=[[CoSIDA]]}} ==Professional Basketball== On March 29, 2010, Aldrich announced that he would forego his final season of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2010 NBA Draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.{{cite news|url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/36087917/ns/sports-college_basketball/|title=Kansas' Cole Aldrich leaving early for NBA|date=March 29, 2010 |publisher=nbcsports.msnbc.com}} The ''[[Sacramento Bee]]'' listed Aldrich as the second best center in the pool, citing his ability as a rebounder, and stated that Aldrich "could be a rotation player immediately". ==See also== * [[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans]] ==References== {{reflist}} == External links == {{commonscat}} *[http://sports.yahoo.com/ncaab/players/72840 Yahoo Sports Profile] *[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=36170 ESPN Profile] {{2008 Kansas basketball}} {{2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Aldrich, Cole}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Minnesota]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Male basketball centers]] [[Category:People from Bloomington, Minnesota]] [[fr:Cole Aldrich]] [[zh:科尔·阿尔德里奇]]
